history.text: Overview Selfoss was settled by Þórir Ásason sometime after 1000, but the sagas of Icelanders mention that Ingólfur Arnarson was there during the winter of 873-74, under the Ingólfsfjall mountain, which is west of.
In the summer of 1891, due to the lobbying of Tryggvi Gunnarsson, a member of the Alþing, the first suspension bridge was built over the Ölfusá.
The largest building is the reconstructed 'Old Dairy' building, a dairy processing plant constructed in 1929 and demolished in 1954, now in use as a food hall.
In 1931, the dairy firm Mjólkurbú Flóamanna and general store Kaupfélag Árnesinga were established.
The current bridge was built in 1945 after the original structure collapsed.
After the construction the building was used for travellers' accommodation and dining, until 1974.

Former World Chess Champion Bobby Fischer is buried near Selfoss at Laugardælir cemetery. 2008 earthquake According to the United States Geological Survey, an earthquake with a moment magnitude of 6.3 occurred near Selfoss on.
A number of sheep in the Selfoss area were killed. New town center In the summer of 2021, a new pedestrianised town center was opened.
As a result of its success, in 2022 it was decided to expand the project with 40 new houses, including two hotels.
